lines:
Implements every StorageFactory, StorageBackend and ReadSnapshot operation over the existing project SQLite file. Owns all production SQL, row mapping, schema/seeding and computer registration in storage/sqlite/. WAL read transactions pin consistent views while atomic immediate write transactions apply validation, resource/readToken guards, changes, versions, receipts and one revision. Schema 14 preserves IDs/history/drafts/legacy receipts and seeds previously unversioned resources. Initialized registered reads are write-free. Desktop and MCP use the shared selecting ProjectStore without Connection access; QA shell execution and local caches stay outside the backend.

Approved Markdown extension (implementation pending): Add a versioned, transactional schema upgrade for project-owned Markdown documents and ordered typed design associations. Implement all new shared snapshot/mutation/resource/reference/token methods in storage/sqlite, including task/QA target resolution, search and readback. Preserve existing IDs, unrelated data, receipts and schema-upgrade rollback. Include new tables in complete snapshot/transfer/schema inventories and reference checks; do not seed duplicate documents on reopen. Existing-token compare, body/metadata update, associations, dependent reference edits, versions, operation receipt and cursor commit atomically. Semantic no-op/retry and initialized read-only access preserve canonical bytes/mtime/revision. Test long Unicode Markdown, exact code fences/newlines, project isolation, stale writes, invalid links, delete protection and rollback.

All-domain numeric ID compatibility (2026-09-25; supersedes the task-only allocator correction): Numeric IDs and human task/QA numbers must retain the pre-adapter SQL behavior in every adapter. Reference baseline is commit f96fca1. All AUTOINCREMENT-backed domains allocate after their highest live, deleted or consumed sequence ID without random gaps; task and QA numbers use the existing project MAX(number)+1 rule. The text adapter restores and retains those sequence high-water marks as existing-format minimal tombstones, including IDs consumed by upserts with no added row, on successful writes and both conversion directions. Centralized sequences.rs is shared by writes and migration; failed transactions, retries and no-ops retain existing semantics. UUID filenames/foreign-key record identities remain internal storage identities; caller-supplied design/note identifiers and opaque concurrency tokens keep their existing contracts. Existing persisted business IDs must not be bulk-renumbered implicitly. Independent clones can collide in any numeric collection; reads report collisions without silently remapping. Conformance compares actual domain allocations, continued writes after upserts and conversion, and every numeric table high-water mark. Future server SQL must implement the same contract instead of introducing a new allocation policy.
